title: New Orleans style versus Texas and Midwest swing bands
summary: Tate says Texas bands were more arranged and swung more than New Orleans Dixieland.

bands.name: T. Holder's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Did you used to think of -- at this
point, did people think of musicians in terms of New Orleans style or Southwest style, Chicago?

I really didn't. You know, I didn't think about -- well, you know, after they started talking about Midwest and Texas and New Orleans style, but I never did think that it actually all started in New Orleans. Maybe it's because when I came up, there were so many good players in Dallas.

There were good -- there were at least about four or five big bands, but good players that never got -- never left. They wouldn't leave, they just stayed right around in Dallas and played like territory bands and things like that. Then there were a lot of musicians that came up from New Orleans to be in Dallas that couldn't carry these cats' instruments and things. But I hadn't gone to New Orleans. Now, New Orleans really did have a little different style. They played more Dixieland than the cats like in Texas. The cats in Texas swung more, you know what I mean?
Did the guys in Texas play that polyphonic thing where you had the clarinet and the trombone and the trumpet, all playing lines at the same time?
See, they played more arrangements. The bands like I heard in Texas, they were more organized like arrangements are and they'd give guys plenty of room to stretch out to take solos.

Then they'd all come back for a great ensemble all together. Now, Dixieland, I would say the New Orleans topped them on Dixieland. But for swing and more organized bands like Blue Devils and Basie and all those kind of bands, you know, I mean like Basie played with Blue Devils and Bennie Moten and T. Holder and bands like -- New Orleans didn't have those kind of bands.
